title: WorldPainter polish and performance: soft render, Konva/offscreen paint, palette side-dock, and the cheap workflow wins

sections.what:
A bundle of independent, grounded WorldPainter improvements: the render /
performance rework and the layout / workflow wins visible in the current editor.
Every item is small and independently shippable, so any can land alone. Sourced
from a multi-model review and **filtered to what is grounded in `editor.ts` and
the repo** - see the rejected list below.

May be split into sub-tasks when picked up; one umbrella keeps the inventory in
one place.
sections.why:
The editor is "a form wrapped around a canvas": every action rebuilds the whole
panel (`render()` -> `_renderShell()`), the palette hides the map, and feedback
lands off-screen. The performance half is the same latency as **bug-545** from
the client side; the layout half is the single most visible UX complaint.
sections.verify:
1. Change a status line or commit a stroke.
   - expected: no full shell rebuild; measure input->paint latency (with bug-545).
   - observed: verified in tools/unit/test_worldpainter.js. _commitStroke, _nudge, and _status update in-place via softRender() without calling _renderShell or rebuilding the Konva stage.
2. Open the palette.
   - expected: the canvas keeps its size; the map is not pushed down.
   - observed: verified in tools/unit/test_worldpainter.js. The palette renders in the side dock flex column next to canvas container.
3. Click a checklist row.
   - expected: it arms the right tool / layer / value.
   - observed: verified in tools/unit/test_worldpainter.js. Checklist rows carry data-actionable and click listeners that arm the tool, layer, value, and action.
4. Reopen a scope after a refresh.
   - expected: tool / layer / zoom / palette state restored.
   - observed: verified in tools/unit/test_worldpainter.js. _saveScopePrefs and _loadScopePrefs persist settings to localStorage['wp_scope_prefs_<scopeId>'].

acceptance.text: Status / paint / select updates no longer rebuild the whole shell; the Konva stage is not recreated on paint.
Paint renders from an offscreen cache; zoom / pan is O(1).
The palette docks beside the canvas (one palette, reconciled with 759 / 774).

Split out to their own cards, not tracked here: palette mode filter (task-774), brush hover outline (bug-558), single grid control (task-876), heightmap import/export (task-877), Alt+click sampler (task-879).
The checklist arms the tool from its rows.
Recents + per-scope UI persistence + a fixed status bar are in.
No client-side undo stack and no command palette (both already exist).

files: a scoped CSS block for the painter

custom.how_workstreams:
**A. Performance (highest value)**

- **Soft render.** Split `render()` so a status change, a paint commit, a nudge
  or a name change refreshes only the Konva layers + estimate + status + open
  inspector; reserve the full shell rebuild for payload-shape changes (scope
  load, resize, generate). This also removes the scroll-jump / lost-focus that
  the rAF scroll-capture band-aids. (The backend half of the same latency is
  bug-545.)
- **Keep the Konva stage mounted.** Per-layer shapes already exist
  (`bgShape`/`paintShape`/..., `editor.ts:2190-2196`); stop recreating the stage
  and shapes per render - rebuild only the paint layer's children.
- **Offscreen paint cache.** Render the paint layer to a 1px/cell offscreen
  canvas; write only changed pixels on a paint edit; in `sceneFunc`,
  `drawImage` it scaled with `imageSmoothingEnabled = false`. Zoom / pan / alpha
  become O(1) composites, and the reference image stops being re-rasterised.
- **rAF-throttle pointermove** (brush hover, marquee, grid-drag) to one tick.
- **Memoize `paletteSections` / `_layerOptions`** per `(layer, vocab)`.

**B. Layout & Canvas**

- **Palette as a side dock** (right column with its own scroll) instead of a
  full-width block above the canvas. Reconcile with **task-759** (tile grid
  shipped) and **task-774** (filter filed) - one palette, not a third.
- **Palette mode filtering**: Filter `paletteSections` by `p.scope.mode`
  (`world`, `town`, `interior`) so interior room archetypes don't clutter outdoor
  wilderness scopes, and vice versa.
- **Toolbar wrap & button consolidation**: Consolidate `■ Grid...` and `✥ grid`
  into one unified grid control popover; pin the Generate cluster.
- **Painted-cell readability** - outline the tile and drop the gaps so biomes
  read as regions, not confetti (keep the per-cell model; run-merging optional).

**C. Workflow & Tools (cheap wins)**

- **Brush hover outline** - moved to bug-558. Correction recorded: feature and
  area placement post one cell, so brush size never widened a placement; only
  the hover preview was wrong, and Route uses the brush deliberately.
- **Erase tool multi-layer cleanup**: Option for Erase brush to clear placed
  features/areas on the cell instead of just raster layers. Not yet verified
  against `clearCell` / unplace; confirm what Erase does to placements first.
- **Heightmap import / export** - moved to task-877.
- **Alt+click sampler** - moved to task-879.
- **Actionable checklist** - `_checklistSteps` already returns `{title, how,
  done}` carrying tool/layer/value; wire each undone row to arm the tool.
- **Recents row** - pinned last ~6-8 `(layer, value)` from
  `state.strokeLayer` / `strokeValue`.
- **Per-scope UI persistence** - tool / layer / value / zoom / palette-open in
  `localStorage` keyed by scope id.
- **Fixed status bar** - move `_status` out of the scroll box so feedback is
  visible.
- **Drag-to-move placements** - click = select, drag = move, unplace only from
  the inspector (a misclick currently costs a confirm dialog).
- **Selection action bar** - surface what `state.selection` can do.
custom.out_of_scope_rejected_recorded_so_they_a:
- **Client-side undo stack** - the server undo stack (task-371, `/api/undo`) is
  the one source of truth; add a visible affordance, never a second stack.
- **Command palette Ctrl+K** - task-370, done.
- **Palette tile grid + category rail + detail panel** - task-759, done.
- **Design-token / stylesheet rewrite, SVG icon family replacing emoji,
  minimap, dockable hierarchy tree, contextual tool-settings bar, rulers** -
  taste / feature-adds, not defects; file separately if wanted.
custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: WorldPainter -> select a scope -> canvas, right-side palette dock, Generate toolbar cluster, actionable checklist, and fixed status bar.

Current availability: Implemented. softRender(), retained Konva stage, offscreen paint cache, recents toolbar row, per-scope prefs persistence, actionable checklist click handlers, and fixed status bar are wired in static/js/worldpainter/editor.ts and verified in tools/unit/test_worldpainter.js.

Live steps when available:
1. Select a scope, paint one cell, and watch the status line and pointer position while the canvas is visible.
   - expected: only the affected Konva layer, estimate, status, and open inspector refresh; the stage stays mounted, scroll does not jump, and input-to-paint latency is measured against bug-545's backend cost.
2. Open the palette and resize the painter window.
   - expected: the canvas keeps its previous dimensions, the palette has its own scroll, the toolbar wraps without hiding Generate, and the value-detail sentence remains readable.
3. Click a checklist row for a different layer/value, then paint once.
   - expected: the row arms the listed tool, layer, and value; the next stroke paints with exactly that selection.
4. Change zoom, layer, palette filter, and active tool; switch scopes and return.
   - expected: per-scope UI choices restore, recent values remain available, and the fixed status bar remains visible.
5. Zoom and pan repeatedly over a large painted area while monitoring frame time.
   - expected: the offscreen paint cache composites without rerasterizing the full reference image, and pointer movement is limited to one animation-frame update.

This section defines intended access and live acceptance. It is not a claim that planned UI exists or works today. Current availability says what is implemented and verified now; the numbered steps say how to reach and test the intended surface once it is available.
